purpose: Determine whether the newly documented dwg-rs public corpus supplies an eligible source witness for the open AC1032 associative-network class-version-2 schema and graph gate.

sources.title: dwg-rs README
observations: The repository describes itself as pre-alpha.
Its README reports five associative-network custom classes among records skipped in four BookViewerApp3 drawings.
The README says those records have no DXF exports and that their few occurrences do not settle the field lists.

sources.title: dwg-rs clean-room corpus record
observations: The documented BookViewerApp3 source pin is commit b8e1dcbf26183e96d199499e491c368c935fb0b0 and is identified as MIT-licensed.
The listed drawings are four AC1014 files: 2d.dwg, 3d.dwg, Draw.dwg, and Draw2.dwg.
The repository attributes AutoCAD authorship to selected R14 files using embedded AutoCAD 2019 installation paths, while noting R14 lacks AcDb:AppInfo.

assessment.reason: The documented BookViewerApp3 candidates are AC1014, not AC1032. The peer repository itself says the associative-class records have no DXF twins and do not settle their field lists.
assessment.producerEvidence: The file corpus is pinned and MIT-licensed; selected embedded product paths are source metadata, not a producer execution receipt or native semantic oracle.
assessment.decision: Keep the AC1032 associative-network schema/output gate open. Retain this only as a possible AC1014 parser-boundary candidate if its exact source files are later inspected; do not use it to infer AC1032 fields or associative behavior.
